Tasks: Multi-domain closed-ended QA: math, physics, biology/medicine, CS, humanities, chemistry, engineering
Description: Expert-vetted, "Google-proof" frontier academic questions meant to be the final closed-ended benchmark; also scores answer calibration, not just accuracy
Statistics: 2,500 public questions + private held-out set; 100+ subjects; some multi-modal (text+image) -> need filter; math ~41% of set
How to run?: Simple I/O eval: zero-shot question ? free-form/exact-match answer + stated confidence ? automated scoring; no sandbox needed. Supported by EvalScope (--datasets hle), official repo
Citation:
Phan et al., "Humanity's Last Exam," 2025, arXiv:2501.14249
(606 citations)

Tasks: Multi-task knowledge + reasoning MCQ across 14 disciplines (STEM, law, psychology, history, etc.)
Description: Harder, less-saturated successor to MMLU; expands to 10 answer choices and requires CoT to reduce guessing and better separate strong models
Statistics: 12,000 questions; 14 disciplines; 10 options/question; standard protocol uses 5-shot
How to run?: Simple I/O eval: 5-shot CoT prompt ? generated reasoning + final letter ? regex-extracted letter ? exact match. Natively supported by lm-evaluation-harness, EvalScope, DeepEval
Citation:
Wang et al., "MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark," 2024, arXiv:2406.01574
(2264 citations)

Tasks: Graduate-level science MCQ: physics, biology, chemistry
Description: Google-proof PhD-level questions; skilled non-experts fail even with web access, designed to test genuine domain reasoning vs. search/recall
Statistics: 198 questions (Diamond subset of 448 main / 546 extended); 4-choice MCQ; random baseline 25%; PhD human baseline ~65-70%
How to run?: Simple I/O eval: zero-shot or 5-shot CoT prompt ? letter answer ? regex/exact match. No sandbox. Supported by lm-eval-harness, EvalScope, official repo
Citation:
Rein et al., "GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark," 2023, arXiv:2311.12022
(3333 citations)

Tasks: Function/tool-calling: single-turn (simple/multiple/parallel), multi-turn, irrelevance detection, live user-contributed
Description: Measures whether a model selects, formats, and executes the correct API/tool call from a natural-language request; de facto standard for tool-use eval
Statistics: 1,700+ function-call examples across categories; continuously updated with live/community data
How to run?: Benchmark-specific harness required (official bfcl-eval PyPI package / Gorilla repo). Deterministic AST-match scoring for most categories (no LLM judge); "Execute" categories run real API calls and compare output
Citation:
Patil et al., "The Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL): From Tool Use to Agentic Evaluation of LLMs," ICML 2025, proceedings.mlr.press/v267/patil25a.html
(591 citations)

Tasks: Long-horizon software engineering tasks (bug fixes/features) across 91 active open-source repos, 5 languages (TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript, Rust)
Description: Contamination-resistant successor to SWE-bench-style benchmarks: every task is an original, hand-written engineering problem (not mined from a merged PR) with a purpose-built functional verifier, specifically designed to fix the solution-leakage and verifier-misgrading issues documented in SWE-bench Pro (8% false positives, 24% false negatives)
Statistics: 113 tasks; 91 repos; 5 languages; reference solutions touch ~5.5� more code than comparable SWE-bench Pro tasks; metrics: pass@1, pass@4
How to run?: Complex setup: isolated per-task container + separate verifier environment (Harbor); works with existing scaffolds (mini-swe-agent is model-agnostic; companion tool "Pier" can also drive Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode); supports parallel sandboxed runs on Modal; agent commits a patch that's applied and graded in a pristine container
Citation: DataCurve/Agentica Team, "DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks," 2026, arXiv:2607.07946

Tasks: Competitive programming (LeetCode/AtCoder/Codeforces-style); also self-repair, code execution, test-output prediction scenarios
Description: Contamination-resistant coding benchmark � problems are timestamped so evaluation can be restricted to problems released after a model's training cutoff, avoiding the leakage seen in HumanEval/MBPP
Statistics: 600+ problems (growing continuously since May 2023); tagged by difficulty (easy/medium/hard) and release date
How to run?: Simple I/O + sandboxed execution: prompt ? generated code ? run against hidden test cases ? pass@1. Official lcb_runner harness needed for exact reproducibility (timeouts, sandboxing, date-window filtering)
Citation:
Jain et al., "LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of LLMs for Code," 2024, arXiv:2403.07974
(1983 citations)

Tasks: Research-level scientific coding: numerical methods, simulation, scientific calculation across physics, math, chemistry, biology, materials science
Description: Scientist-curated benchmark converting real research scripts into decomposed coding subproblems; tests combining domain knowledge with code synthesis, including compounding multi-step "main problems"
Statistics: 80 main problems ? 338 subproblems (288 in test set); 16 subfields; optional "with scientific background" mode
How to run?: Simple I/O per subproblem + sandboxed execution: prompt (+ prior subproblem code, +/- background) ? generated function ? run vs. scientist-annotated unit tests. Main-problem score requires ALL subproblems + final integration correct. Official harness on GitHub
Citation:
Tian et al., "SciCode: A Research Coding Benchmark Curated by Scientists," NeurIPS 2024 D&B, arXiv:2407.13168
(185 citations)

Tasks: Long-horizon, enterprise-grade software engineering: multi-file bug fixes + feature additions requiring substantial code changes across business apps, B2B services and developer tools (Python, Go, TypeScript, JavaScript)
Description: Harder, contamination-resistant successor to SWE-bench from Scale AI, built for realistic enterprise problems. Tasks are mined from consecutive real commits (a fix/feature commit + the tests that demonstrate it), then human-verified and augmented with requirements + interface specs so they stay resolvable. Uses copyleft/GPL public repos plus private commercial startup repos to resist solution leakage; frontier models still score only ~23% (GPT-5 23.3%, Claude Opus 4.1 23.1%)
Statistics: 1,865 human-verified tasks across 41 actively maintained repos, split into Public (731 instances / 11 copyleft repos, released on HuggingFace), Held-out (12 repos, results not published) and Commercial (18 private startup repos). Each task ships fail2pass + pass2pass tests; metric = Pass@1; agents run with a 250-turn limit and uncapped cost
How to run?: Complex containerized harness, but provided in the repo: prebuilt per-instance Docker images on Docker Hub (jefzda/sweap-images, a dockerhub_tag per dataset row) + SWE-agent as the default model-agnostic scaffold (Git submodule; model set via a YAML config e.g. claude.yaml; supports API models and local vLLM). Flow: run SWE-agent to generate patches -> helper_code/gather_patches.py compiles predictions -> swe_bench_pro_eval.py applies + grades each patch in a pristine container. Modal recommended for parallelism (beta --use_local_docker for local); needs a Docker Hub username
Link: Leaderboard: labs.scale.com/leaderboard/swe_bench_pro_public - OS repo: github.com/scaleapi/SWE-bench_Pro-os - Data (public set): huggingface.co/datasets/ScaleAI/SWE-bench_Pro
Citation: Deng et al. (Scale AI), "SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?," 2025, arXiv:2509.16941 (recent - Sep 2025, citations still accumulating)
